extraction_scope: worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism adjudication from source text and figures; automated nucleic-acid/cell-wall placeholder claims removed.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Time-of-addition assays support direct interaction with viral particles as a major mechanism for HSV and several enveloped viruses; cell pre/post-treatment was weaker, with paramyxovirus behavior explicitly treated as an exception.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: TL, TL1, and TL-derived analogs tested in this paper
mechanism_claims.limitations: Direct virion interaction is supported by time-of-addition infectivity assays, not by direct biophysical measurement of membrane rupture in this paper.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Lipidated TL6 analogs, especially N-terminal cholesterol/fatty-acid variants, show improved antiviral potency and reduced cytotoxicity in the recovered tables; the paper interprets this as facilitated membrane/bilayer association.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Mechanistic class is inferred from source structure-activity discussion and antiviral/cytotoxicity tables, not promoted to a direct membrane-disruption assay.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The discussion proposes viral-envelope lipid bilayer disruption or pore formation as a plausible explanation for broad enveloped-virus selectivity; this remains a source-stated mechanistic hypothesis.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: TL peptide class and enveloped virus activity
mechanism_claims.limitations: No cell-wall or nucleic-acid mechanism is accepted for this antiviral paper; membrane/envelope damage language is bounded as hypothesis unless tied to time-of-addition infectivity evidence.
